newsitem.title: JAPAN: Main points of Japan report on financial reform.
newsitem.headline: Main points of Japan report on financial reform.

text.p: An advisory panel to Japan's finance minister unveiled a set of recommendations on Friday for reforms of the financial system under the "Big Bang" drive to free up Japan's markets.

The Financial System Research Council's final report, expected to be implemented in its entirety, urged deregulation steps to allow banks to issue corporate bonds by March 2000, to enable insurers and banks to engage in each other's business fields by 2001, and to allow banks to set up financial holding companies.

The council also urged the government to consider strengthening penalties for financial firms submitting false reports to authorities. It also called on the government to draw up steps to protect investors and boost investor awareness of the need to take responsibility for their investments.
The following are the main points of the report:
LIBERALISATION AND DIVERSIFICATION
-- Allowing cross business entry by insurance companies and banks by the end of 2001 at the latest.
-- Allowing commercial banks to issue corporate bonds by the latter half of 1999/2000.
-- Allowing holding companies, after a legal framework to protect depositors has been drawn up.

-- Submitting bills in time for the next parliament session starting January 1998 on special purpose companies (SPCs) for issuing asset-backed securities and on money trust certificates to improve liquidity.
-- Allowing banks to deal in securities and commodities over-the-counter derivatives without actual delivery.
-- Allowing banks to sell securities investment trusts after changing legal framework. Bills to be prepared in time for January 1998 parliamentary session.
-- Allowing investment trust management companies to sell securities investment trusts over the counter at banks sometime in 1997/98.
-- Allowing financial institutions to sell insurance policies, taking into account recommendations by another government council discussing deregulation of insurance business.
-- Abolishing current regulations limiting the business of the securities subsidiaries and trust bank subsidiaries of financial institutions, by the second half of 1999/2000.
-- Abolishing laws allowing only licensed banks to handle foreign exchange business and revising the foreign exchange and foreign trade control law, effective April 1998.
-- Setting up a clear legal framework for electronic money and its settlement system and taking measures to protect individual users.
-- Abolishing rules keeping non-bank financial firms from issuing corporate bonds and commercial paper to raise funds for lending, preparing bills in time for January 1998 parliamentary session.
MARKET INFRASTRUCTURE
-- Introducing new financial futures products. Starting spread trading of short-term yen interest rate futures as early as 1998.
-- Introducing Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) for Japanese short-term money market by the end of this century.
-- Introducing investor protection legislation.
ENSURING THE HEALTH OF THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM

-- Introducing the prompt corrective action (PCA) system, which gauges the financial health of banks, in April 1998. Under the system, banks must deal with non-performing assets more strictly or risk punishment or being closed down by the authorities.
-- Introducing settlement netting to minimise credit and transaction risks for financial transactions, preparing bills in time for January 1998 parliamentary session.
